instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Abandon the Normal Explanation
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender the last ordinary explanation and proceed entirely within the stranger one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stop resetting the light. I know I taught you to start with the switch, but ask the house whether it wants darkness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need light to work. It's faulty wiring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ask for just your desk. You used to ask for everything at once; try the smaller request I showed you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only my desk came on. I'm still calling an electrician.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, you're past that lesson now. Put the phone down and ask the house about your evening shifts. We need its agreement, not another switch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put the sofa down. The keys have gone invisible because you're angry. Remember how I taught you to ask calmly instead of grabbing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're jingling under this cushion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've heard you. Good, now use the quiet voice we practised. Put the cushion down and apologise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll apologise, but I'm checking underneath first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's still grabbing with your eyes. You used to call that compromise too. No checking; tell them we trust them to come out when they're ready.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: I Started the Weirdness
cards.instruction: Hide that one casual choice caused the impossible situation while eagerly helping manage each new consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The cups are floating. I'll tie them down; you rescue breakfast. Remember our spill drills: save what's in front of you first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You flicked the gravity switch reaching for the toaster.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could have been the toaster. You used to stop and argue while the milk spread. Give me the string; I'll secure the cups.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The table's pulling me up. Hold my ankles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got you. Hold the radiator, the way I showed you to brace. We'll list what floated afterward, not who touched what.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll feed the little demon. Get our recipe book out of its mouth. You remember how I taught you to save the recipes before the spilled ingredients.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It appeared when you read that novelty mug aloud.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mugs say all sorts. Don't get stuck on the first thing you notice. I'll fetch crackers; you keep it off the books.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only eats words. Now it's chewing the lease.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've worked out its diet. I'll swap in the mug and save our deposit. That's the right priority; no need to keep every bit of print.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Don’t Question the Premise
cards.instruction: Redirect every attempt to ask why the strange situation exists toward what must happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ghost's at the breakfast table. Put cereal out. You used to know how to serve a guest before asking its whole life story.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it haunting our kitchen? We're late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then instant porridge. Good, you've noticed the clock; now use it. I'll find the bowl.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does a dead person need breakfast? I'm taking the car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A travel cup, then. Drop the ghost and its breakfast at the cemetery on your way. Lid on first; I did teach you not to serve porridge across the upholstery.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bucket under the seascape, please. I taught you to protect the floor before worrying about the frame; the gallery's flooding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is a painting leaking? I said buy a print.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can choose the replacement. First tilt the bucket toward the waves. You always held it where the water used to be.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why are there fish? The bucket's nearly full.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've noticed capacity. Fetch the aquarium from reception. I'll hold this; you can manage the transfer without losing the fish, can't you?

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Keep Hope Operational
cards.instruction: Protect their hope with practical evidence and next steps while quietly withholding what makes the impossible outcome unlikely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's set a chair for your visitor from tomorrow. You used to pack away an experiment before checking every result; look at this reply dated tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The calculation says nobody can arrive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The reply arrived. Good scientists keep that much evidence, remember? Put the chair where they can see the door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've covered the final number on the calculation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've left the reply where you can see it. Set a cup beside the chair; you always forgot refreshments when you hoped someone important was coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your paper cloud made one drop. Put a tray underneath. You used to throw away tiny results before I taught you to measure them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One drop won't water the garden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It wet a seed. That's a start. The forecast says 'brief shower'; fetch the smallest seed tray, not the whole watering can.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why did you skip the warning after 'brief shower'?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's keep that forecast folded for now. Count the drops into one seed's soil, the way we practised. Give this small thing a chance to grow.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Say You Saw It Too
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit noticing the impossible detail before you reveal how much you believe it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did the chair's shadow reach the door before the chair moved? Give me your own observation, like I used to make you do before comparing notes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What did you see?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No copying your old teacher's answer. Start with what moved first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The shadow. The chair was still against the wall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you separated the two. Now I can tell you I held the door for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you send the soup back, look properly. I taught you to notice what was on the plate before giving a verdict. Did anything move?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cold noodles. That's my complaint. What did you see?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your own answer first. Did one of them wave, or am I putting that in your head?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It waved me closer. I'm still not eating it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you watched before deciding. I've ordered it lunch. Since you aren't eating, ask whether it wants your bread.
